items.title: AI Can Build Your UI. Now Figma Can Tell It When It Screwed Up.
items.summary: AI can now build a UI in seconds, but that doesn't mean it built the UI you actually designed. A new Applitools integration turns Figma designs into visual baselines, automatically catching the subtle differences AI coding agents leave behind before they make it into production.

items.title: 25 Places Designers Can Still Find Free, Non-AI Images for Commercial Use
items.summary: AI images are taking over stock libraries, but the human-made web isn't dead yet. We found 25 places where designers can still find incredible free, real photography, art, and imagery for commercial use.

items.title: Chrome Can Now Measure Exactly How Obnoxious Your Website’s Ads Are
items.summary: Chrome can now measure exactly how obnoxious a website’s ads are, from how much of your screen they swallow to how much data and CPU time they burn. Those ad-stuffed websites can finally be measured, and the results are public.

items.title: Cloudflare Just Gave AI Training Bots the Middle Finger
items.summary: Cloudflare just gave website owners a new weapon against AI crawlers: keep the search traffic, block the AI training. After years of watching bots consume the web’s content, publishers finally have an easier way to tell AI companies where to go.

items.title: Today, WordPress Ended a 16-Year Tradition… Meet Ipsum!
items.summary: After 16 years, WordPress just killed one of its most recognizable traditions. The predictable “Twenty Something” default themes are history, and their replacement, Ipsum, signals a surprisingly different vision for what WordPress thinks a modern website should start with.

items.title: Adobe Is Turning Photoshop Elements Into a Much Smarter Photoshop Lite
items.summary: Photoshop Elements is getting a serious AI upgrade, with Generative Expand, AI upscaling and a new assistant that helps you edit simply by describing what you want.

items.title: Web-Perf Wednesday 009 – CrUX Makes Ad Weight Public
items.summary: CrUX adds public ad count, density, CPU, and network metrics, giving publishers and advertisers a shared view of real ad weight.

items.title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Has a Left-Handed Problem
items.summary: Apple moved key controls to the side of its new foldable iPhone to make them easier to reach — but easier for whom? The decision raises a surprisingly big UX question that every web and interface designer should be thinking about.

items.title: I wish you the best in the Offline
items.summary: A handful of people I follow and know about have announced their recent departure. Not from a job (although plenty of that going around), but from social media, AI usage, or in more extreme cases the Internet entirely. In Goodbye, Forever, Probably, Salma announced her retiremen…

items.title: Figma Is Turning Designers Into Plugin Makers
items.summary: Figma is turning a wild idea into reality: instead of searching for the perfect plugin, you can just ask AI to build it. If this catches on, designers may stop choosing the tools in their software—and start inventing them on demand.

items.title: After 53 Years at Monotype, She Got the Ultimate Retirement Gift: Her Own Font
items.summary: After 53 years working with type, Pat Lightizer got the ultimate retirement gift: her own font.

items.title: TikTok Is Quietly Putting Web Apps Inside Its App
items.summary: TikTok isn’t just hosting videos anymore—it’s quietly letting web-based experiences live inside the app. TikTok Minis could blur the line between social network, browser, and app platform, and web designers should be paying attention.

items.title: Google Is Testing a Search Bar That Works Outside Chrome
items.summary: Google is quietly testing a way to bring Search outside Chrome and directly on top of whatever app you’re using. It’s called Project Loom, and this little floating search box could hint at a much bigger future where Google follows you around your desktop.

items.summary: Code Snack by Lauren Basser looks very useful. Engineering concepts for visual learners. Updated weekly. She's breaking down the Terminal, Git, and things like Web Components for people coming from a design background. We've seen a slew of designers swimming in new waters, so re…

items.title: Firefox Is Getting Its Biggest Redesign in Years. Then Mozilla Got Cold Feet.
items.summary: Firefox is getting its biggest makeover in years—but Mozilla has already backed away from some of its boldest ideas. Project Nova reveals what happens when modern design trends, millions of opinionated users, and the internet’s unstoppable obsession with rounded corners collide.

items.title: Meta Just Launched an AI That Uses Websites for You. That Could Be a Big Deal for Web Designers
items.summary: Your website’s next visitor might not be human. Meta’s new Muse agent can navigate sites, fill out forms and take action for you—and it could force web designers to rethink exactly who they’re designing for.

items.title: Web-Perf Wednesday 008 – Good INP Rates Keep Falling
items.summary: CrUX shows another fall in good INP experiences, making careful attribution more useful than a quick explanation.

items.title: Adobe Has a Secret New Design Tool—and You Can Apply to Test It
items.summary: Adobe is quietly testing a mysterious new web-based design tool called Project Oasis—and designers can apply to get inside. Details are scarce, the beta is under NDA, and Adobe isn’t showing much yet… which only makes us want in more.

items.title: The Ampersand Is Nearly 2,000 Years Old — And Designers Still Can’t Agree How It Should Look
items.summary: The ampersand is nearly 2,000 years old. yet designers still can’t agree on what it should look like. From ancient Roman *et* to hundreds of wildly different & designs, the story behind typography’s favorite squiggle is stranger than you might expect.

items.title: Canva Is Quietly Publishing Nearly 1 Million Websites a Month
items.summary: Canva isn't just for presentations and social posts anymore. Nearly 1 million websites are now being published through Canva every month—and with 100+ new Visual Suite updates, web designers may want to start paying attention.

items.title: Instagram’s New Logo Has a Legibility Problem
items.summary: Instagram just redesigned its iconic wordmark—but there’s a problem: a surprising number of people think it says “Instagzam.” The controversy offers a perfect lesson in what happens when brand personality collides with one of design’s most basic rules: people still need to be ab…

items.title: The omitEmpty Function
items.summary: Conditional spreads and if-statements bury the shape of an object. omitEmpty strips the empty values out instead, so you can write an optional property as if it were always there. Here's what counts as empty, and when to go shallow.

items.title: Speaking Without Inhibition
items.summary: Sometimes it's not appropriate to say something. But if you censor yourself all the time, you're being subjugated by other people's opinions — and your ability to speak freely is a measure of how free you really are.
